mainTopic: Why the last line of a שטר is not trusted: רב עמרם's rule that we do not learn new details from the final line (אין למדין משיטה אחרונה), and his proof from a ברייתא about blank lines between the text and the witnesses.
overview: The גמרא had just taught that the last line of a שטר should only repeat what is already written above it. רב עמרם explains why: we never take new information from the last line, because the holder of the document might have added it dishonestly. רב נחמן asks him for a source. רב עמרם brings a ברייתא. If the witnesses signed two lines below the text, the document is פסול. If they signed only one line below, it is כשר. He points out that a forger could write in one blank line just as easily as in two. So the difference only makes sense if the last line is ignored anyway. With one blank line, any forgery would land in the last line, which nobody relies on. With two blank lines, a forger could write a fake line and then a last line repeating it, so the fake detail would be trusted. The גמרא agrees: שמע מינה.

steps.title: רב עמרם: we do not learn from the last line
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם explains the earlier rule: the last line of a document must only repeat earlier content, because no new information is ever learned from the final line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: It is because we do not learn anything from the last line.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם gives the reason behind the earlier rule that a document's last line should only review what is already written in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the person holding the document may have slipped an extra line in between the text and the witnesses' signatures. So any new detail found only in the last line is simply ignored. That is why the last line should contain nothing new, only a repeat of the main points.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not learn (we don't draw information from it)
the last line of the document

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains how documents are written and read: the final line carries no independent weight.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the earlier rule that the last line must repeat the document's content.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new information may be taken from the final line of a document, since it may have been added by the holder.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב עמרם where he knows this rule from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב עמרם: Where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks for a source for רב עמרם's rule. This sets up the next move, where רב עמרם brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן is not attacking the rule. He wants to know what earlier source it rests on.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you know this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב עַמְרָם:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Amram:
From where do you know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב עמרם's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that we do not learn from the last line.

steps.title: The ברייתא about blank lines before the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם quotes a ברייתא: if the witnesses signed two lines below the text, the document is פסול; if one line below, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: As a ברייתא teaches: If the witnesses were placed two lines away from the text, the document is invalid. If only one line away, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם brings a ברייתא as his source. It contrasts a two-line gap (פסול) with a one-line gap (כשר).
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, the ברייתא just seems to be about blank space where someone could add fake text. רב עמרם will next show that this simple reading does not explain the difference between one line and two.

keyTerms.meaning: the written text of the document

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is taught:

phrases.notes: He means the witnesses' signatures were placed lower down, leaving blank lines.

phrases.english: two lines from the text, it is invalid;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's question by citing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not learn from the last line.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a two-line gap before the witnesses makes the document פסול, while a one-line gap leaves it כשר.

steps.title: Why should one line be different from two?
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם points out that the forgery worry exists equally with one blank line, so the simple reading cannot explain the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about two lines? If it's because he might forge and write something there, then with one line too he could forge and write something!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם analyzes the ברייתא and raises a difficulty with reading it simply. This prepares the way for his conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only worry were that the holder fills a blank space with fake text, a single blank line is just as dangerous as two. So the ברייתא's lenient ruling on one line needs a different explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against רב עמרם. It is רב עמרם himself showing that the ברייתא only makes sense according to his rule.

phrases.english: What is different about two lines?
That perhaps he will forge and write something there;
with one line also, he could forge and write something!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted and shows that its plain reading leaves a gap.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the ברייתא, that a gap is invalid only because of forgery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forgery is equally possible in one blank line, so forgery alone cannot explain why one line is כשר and two are פסול.

steps.title: So we do not learn from the last line: proven
steps.stepSummary: The only explanation is that the last line is ignored anyway, which proves רב עמרם's rule. The גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that we do not learn from the last line? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם concludes that the ברייתא proves his rule, and the גמרא confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one blank line, a forged line would become the last line, and nobody learns from the last line, so it does no harm. With two blank lines, a forger could write a fake detail in the first line and a repeat of it in the last line. Then the fake detail is no longer in the last line, so it would be trusted. That is why only two lines make the document פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it, it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: אין למדין משיטה אחרונה: the last line of a document is never trusted for new information. The proof is that a one-line gap before the witnesses is כשר, because anything written there would be the last line and ignored.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains both why a one-line gap is tolerated and why a document's last line must only repeat earlier content.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that we learn from this
that we do not learn from the last line?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty from step 4 by applying רב עמרם's rule, which completes the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא proves that new information is never taken from the last line of a document.
